bottom_line: Neither Z13 nor Z32 is solved. No proposed text for either beats a fair null model, and every published proposal we could test is incompatible with the cipher or indistinguishable from chance. The binding limit is information, not computation. Z13 is probably not an ordinary English phrase under plain substitution without errors, and its repeat pattern is atypical of Zodiac's Z408/Z340-style keys. The one lead (Z340 key letters on Z13's six shared symbols, family-wise p about 0.005-0.01 within its task) did not hold up: the pre-registered replication gave 0.039 over its 12 tests, failed its negative control (the Z408 key does about as well on n-gram statistics), and is not significant at project scale. It is a negative result and yields no meaningful text (results/lead/DECISION.md).

novel_findings: Quantification, not a new idea (Pelling 2017 argued it qualitatively; Oranchak 2012 showed no window of the solved ciphers is as repetitive): Z13's repeat pattern is atypical of Zodiac-style cycled homophonic keys: 0 of 20,000 phrases reproduce its 8-symbol profile; Bayes factor 10^2.7-10^3.8 for a mostly one-symbol-per-letter key (direction robust, strength model-dependent).

New calibration (the phrase IN THE DESERT IS was listed by Oranchak in 2012): an ordinary-English plain-substitution Z13 text would rank among the few dozen most fluent fits (median rank 2; Zodiac's own text median 58 of 4.15M); those fits are fragments, so that hypothesis is disfavoured (judgement in the last step).

Not new (corrected after the prior-art search): the Mt. Diablo inset figures (true north 4.6 deg clockwise of map-up; scale bar about 9% too long, 7.0-7.2 ground mi per paper inch) were published first by shaqmeister (forum, 2026-05-12); this project only confirms them independently. Several published instructions fall off the mailed piece.

Negative result, not a finding (corrected after the lead investigation): the Z340-key letters on Z13 looked English-friendly within the task (family-wise p 0.005-0.01), but the pre-registered replication gave 0.039 over 12 tests, failed its negative control, and is not significant at project scale. No evidence of key reuse (results/lead/DECISION.md).
